title: The Marshall Plan — Economic Aid as Cold War Strategy

documents.label: A
documents.citation: Secretary of State George C. Marshall, Commencement Address at Harvard University, June 5, 1947 — U.S. government document, available through the Avalon Project, Yale Law School
documents.excerpt: It is logical that the United States should do whatever it is able to do to assist in the return of normal economic health in the world, without which there can be no political stability and no assured peace. Our policy is directed not against any country or doctrine but against hunger, poverty, desperation, and chaos. Any government that is willing to assist in the task of recovery will find full co-operation... on the part of the United States Government. Any government which maneuvers to block the recovery of other countries cannot expect help from us.

documents.label: B
documents.citation: Soviet Foreign Minister Vyacheslav Molotov, Statement rejecting the Marshall Plan, Paris Conference, July 2, 1947 — diplomatic record, available through the Avalon Project, Yale Law School
documents.excerpt: The American plan splits Europe into two groups of states and creates new difficulties in the relations between them... The Marshall plan, which envisages for American credits various conditions infringing on the sovereignty of European countries and interfering in their home affairs... will lead to nothing but a further aggravation of relations between countries.
